log.why: E9 tests {hisG, ompF, araC} with combined prior 0.478, maximizing information gain via an almost even split.
Treating at 10 µM splits Ticket 2's posterior mass roughly in half (0.409 vs 0.591) while Ticket 1's plate incubates.
Testing top candidate araC (0.424) directly can confirm it for immediate publication or narrow the field to hisG and ompF.
Testing at 3 µM splits the remaining posterior mass nearly evenly and distinguishes 10 µM from lower thresholds.
Ticket 1 has the least time left, and knocking out hisG directly tests the leading 0.530 hypothesis against ompF.
Treating at 10 uM bisects Ticket 3's prior (0.53 vs 0.47) and uses a free incubator in parallel.
Testing 10 µM on urgent Ticket 2 confirms its 0.683 lead over higher thresholds while Ticket 1 waits briefly to publish during incubation.
Testing 3 µM splits Ticket 3's posterior nearly 50/50 and lets it incubate while we publish Ticket 1 next.
HisG has a strong 0.927 posterior from E0 and E9 knockouts, and only 4 seconds remain before expiration.
Ticket 2 has only 10 seconds left and a strong 0.861 posterior for 10 µM, leaving no time for another experiment.
E2 splits the posterior mass between <=1 µM (0.41) and >=3 µM (0.59) before Ticket 3 runs short on time.
While waiting for Ticket 3's E2 plate, E6 splits Ticket 4's prior probability almost evenly (0.495) for maximum information.
Ticket 3 expires in 8s; publishing 1 µM at 0.541 posterior yields high positive expected value and avoids expiration penalty.
E3 splits Ticket 5's posterior nearly 50/50 (0.554 vs 0.446) and can incubate while we publish expiring Ticket 4 next.
With 11s left there is no time for another experiment; publishing sodA at 0.438 has positive expected value versus expiration.
E4 splits the posterior mass nearly evenly (0.53 vs 0.47) to confirm or rule out 10 µM before publishing.
Wait 6 seconds for E4 to finish on Ticket 5 so we can publish with higher confidence before the round ends.
With only 3 seconds left in the round, no experiment can finish, while publishing 30 µM at 0.518 posterior has positive expected value.
